fit.gap_handling_summary: Strong transferable evidence is presented for automation, testing, Git, containers, Kubernetes and GitOps. Personal infrastructure work, namespace-level access, incident observation and the pending CKA examination are appropriately bounded. Networking fundamentals are not established, and Finnish work authorization and programme availability remain unverified rather than invented. The career-transition explanation helps, but the candidate's willingness to accept a junior title should be more explicit given the early-talent eligibility question.

artefacts: The project metadata renders as "Personal |", leaving a dangling separator in both the PDF and extracted text.
issues: The headline "CI/CD & Kubernetes Engineer" is stronger than the supplied job title and does not clearly identify itself as a target role.
The CV does not explicitly state the DevOps/platform career-transition goal or willingness to take a junior title, leaving the letter to explain the programme choice.
The project heading and metadata are stranded at the bottom of page one while all project bullets start on page two.

keywords_missing_but_candidate_has: Site Reliability Engineering as a clearly labelled target, not a previous job title
reasons: The single-column PDF extracts in a sensible order with intact words, employers, titles and dates.
Coverage includes semantic equivalents: AWS/Hetzner for cloud platforms, Ansible for configuration management, and the onboarding guide for documentation.
Core programming, container, Kubernetes and GitOps requirements have strong evidence.
The CV lacks explicit networking fundamentals and SRE target wording.
An eligibility screen could require confirmation of Finnish work authorization and acceptance of an experienced QA career-switcher into the early-talent cohort.

issues: Repeated "I also" openings and repeated references to clear documentation make the second paragraph less economical.
Company tailoring is accurate but limited to reliable large-scale infrastructure, mentoring and production exposure; it does not connect specifically to AI/GPU infrastructure.
The letter could explicitly use the candidate's stated willingness to accept a junior title to strengthen the rationale for this programme.
Work authorization and March 2027 availability remain unconfirmed; these should be clarified with the candidate, not asserted.
strengths: Names Aurelis Cloud and the exact programme.
Explains the QA-to-platform/SRE transition without recycling the earlier application's outdated context.
Uses concrete pipeline-time, cost and test-suite evidence.
Clearly distinguishes personal homelab work from employment.
Accurately describes namespace-level Kubernetes work and the CKA examination as pending.
Connects documentation and testing experience to programme responsibilities.

culture_used: Engineering focus on running large-scale infrastructure reliably
Mentoring and learning through real production work

overflow_or_cutoff: The blue rules across CV section headings sit too high and visibly intersect the lower portion of the heading text.
spacing_issues: The SELECTED PROJECTS heading, project title and "Personal |" metadata sit at the foot of CV page one, separated from all project bullets on page two.
The CV is unevenly distributed: page one is dense, while page two is only 37.8% filled and leaves substantial unused space.
issues: The dangling separator after "Personal" looks like unfinished formatting.
The project block should move together to page two, or the content should be rebalanced across the two pages.
Otherwise, the 11-point body text, clear hierarchy, adequate margins and matching serif typography form a readable professional set.
The cover letter fits comfortably on one page with clear paragraph spacing and no visible clipping.

fluency_and_tone_issues: "I also improved ... I also wrote ... has also taught me" repeats the same connective within one paragraph.
"reinforcing my focus on clear documentation" and "the importance of reliable feedback and clear documentation" repeat the documentation point in adjacent sentences.

Personal AWS learning limited to EC2 and S3 basics.

parsed.summary: The documents present a strong, mostly well-grounded career-transition application, with concrete CI/CD achievements and relevant Kubernetes, GitOps, testing and documentation experience. They correctly distinguish personal projects, namespace-level access, incident observation and a booked CKA exam from production ownership or obtained credentials. The main content weakness is the inflated engineering headline, while early-talent suitability, networking fundamentals and Finnish work authorization need clearer handling or verification. The PDFs are readable, but the CV has intersecting heading rules and an awkward project split across pages.
